Kuvitus: talvinen iltahämärä maaseudulla: Illustration: a winter dusk in the countryside. In the middle is a red wooden house with snow on its roof and light in its windows. On the gable wall of the house is a satellite dish aimed low into the sky on the left. A faint dashed line runs from the dish to a television satellite with two solar panels in the sky. The satellite is on a dashed arc that crosses the sky. There are stars in the sky, the edge of a forest in the background and snowbanks and spruces in front.
Kaavakuva pohjoisnavan suunnasta, säteet: Diagram seen from the direction of the North Pole, radii to scale. In the middle is the Earth, round which the geostationary orbit runs as a dashed line. The radius r of the orbit is about 42 200 km, about 6.6 Earth radii. The Earth rotates and the satellite orbits in the same direction, anticlockwise, and each makes one revolution in the time T = 23 h 56 min. The blue velocity arrow of the satellite is along the tangent of the orbit, and the red arrow of the gravitational force points to the centre of the Earth. On the Earth's surface is the position of the dish, from which a dashed line runs to the satellite. Six hours later the dish and the satellite have each turned a quarter of a revolution: the new line of sight, drawn faintly, is the same line turned.
Kolme voimakuviota allekkain. Ylimpänä t: Three free-body diagrams one below the other. At the top a uniform plank at rest on two supports, drawn as a rectangle: the weight G starts from the centre and points down, and the normal forces N 1 and N 2 point up from the lower surface. Support 2 is closer to the centre, and its normal force is twice as long as N 1; together they are as long as the weight. Conditions: the sum of the forces and the sum of the moments are zero. In the middle a car at the top of a hump, drawn as a rectangle: the weight G down and the normal force N up, shorter than the weight. Beside the car a blue velocity arrow forwards and an orange acceleration arrow down towards the centre of the curve. Condition: G minus N is m v squared divided by r. At the bottom a satellite drawn as a rectangle: the only force is the gravitational force F of the Earth, down towards the centre of the Earth. Beside it a velocity arrow forwards and an acceleration arrow down. Condition: the gravitational force is m v squared divided by r.
Kuvaaja: langan voima F newtoneina kierr: Graph: the force F of the string in newtons as a function of the period T in seconds. Seven black points at the periods 0.60–1.50 s, forces from 5.42 N to 0.88 N. A dashed curve runs through the points, falling steeply at short periods and levelling off at long ones: the force decreases faster than the period grows, so a straight line does not fit the points.
Kuvaaja: langan voima F newtoneina suure: Graph: the force F of the string in newtons as a function of the quantity one divided by T squared, in the unit one divided by second squared. Seven black points between 0.44 and 2.78, forces from 0.88 N to 5.42 N. A rising straight line fitted to the points passes almost through the origin. The line is extended as a dashed line up to the force 8.0 N, which is the strength of the string; it is reached when one divided by T squared is about 4.1. Two points on the line are circled, (0.50; 1.01) and (2.50; 4.91), from which the slope of about 1.95 N s² is read.
Käsitekartta. Ylhäällä solmu: voimakuvio: Concept map. At the top is the node: the free-body diagram first, then Newton's second law sum F = m a. Three branches lead down from it. Equilibrium: moment M = F r, the sum of the forces is zero, so the body does not move off, and the sum of the moments is zero, so it does not turn. Circular motion: orbital speed v = omega r, the centripetal acceleration a n = v squared divided by r points to the centre, and in the equation of motion the net force gives the centripetal acceleration. Gravitation: the attractive force F g = gamma m 1 m 2 divided by r squared, the weight G = m g as vectors, and for a satellite the gravitational force gives the centripetal acceleration.
Voimakuvio, ei lukuarvoja: auto vaakasuo: Free-body diagram, no numerical values: a car in a curve of a horizontal road seen from behind, as a rectangle. The centre of the curve is to the left. The weight G starts from the centre point and points down, and the normal force N, equally long, starts from the road surface and points up. The road surface is a dashed line. The friction force F mu starts from the lower left corner of the car and points to the left along the road, towards the centre of the curve. Beside the car an orange acceleration arrow points to the left towards the centre. The velocity points away from the viewer, drawn as a circle with a cross inside.
